answer: Picture a newcomer queue where every fresh identity must first spend a week doing unpaid cross-checking. Its arrival gets stamped into a public log, so a batch born in the same minute shows up as one obvious cluster. A lone trader who wandered in from the mesa cannot hide inside that crowd; its stamp stands by itself. Operators read those stamps like a relic of provenance — dull, old, but genuinely hard to forge. The trusted grove meanwhile grows one verified task at a time, and each new branch must be grafted on by a member who stakes their own standing.
